outcome.rationale: Trial designed to characterize antibody kinetics, not test hypothesis against threshold. Success depends on completing longitudinal measurements and achieving stratification by immunosenescence markers. No results available by cutoff; observational design limits definitive outcome classification.

primary_rollup.rule: success=全部主要终点yes；fail=任一主要终点no；其余uncertain
primary_rollup.binarize_rule: uncertain 且 P>=0.5 记 yes、P<0.5 记 no 后再聚合（阈值缺失时的兜底口径，非模型原始判断）

value.uncertainty: No direct baseline data; wide variability expected based on infection timing and severity; immunosenescence heterogeneity
value.rationale: Baseline titers in seropositive elderly nursing home residents highly variable depending on infection recency and severity. Based on Collarino 2022 patterns, expect detectable NAb in most with wide range.

value.estimand: COVID-19 positive residents at 3 months post-baseline
value.uncertainty: Indirect evidence only; Collarino shows stability from month 3 but individual variability high; no direct 3-month results for this cohort
value.rationale: At 3 months, NAb titers in elderly LTCF residents remain detectable in majority. Collarino 2022 shows 82% had anti-S >75 U/mL at some point; expect modest decline from baseline but persistence.

value.estimand: COVID-19 positive residents at 6 months post-baseline
value.uncertainty: Collarino shows significant NAb decline between month 3-6; immunosenescence accelerates waning; proportion with titers >50 AU/mL drops substantially
value.rationale: Significant decline expected between 3-6 months per Collarino 2022. Elderly immunosenescent population shows faster antibody waning. Estimate ~50-60% maintain detectable NAb, fewer maintain high titers.

value.estimand: COVID-19 positive residents at 9 months post-baseline
value.uncertainty: Limited 9-month data in elderly; extrapolation from 6-12 month patterns; high inter-individual variability; immunosenescence effects
value.rationale: Based on plateau pattern observed after month 6 in Collarino 2022, expect titers to stabilize but remain lower than peak. ~50% may retain detectable NAb at 9 months, but levels variable.

analysis_trace.trial_identification: NCT04563650 (SERO-CoV-OLD) is a prospective observational study of COVID-19 neutralizing antibody kinetics in elderly nursing home residents (EHPAD/USLD) at Amiens CHU, France. Design: parallel, non-randomized comparison between COVID-19 positive and negative residents. Primary endpoints: neutralizing antibody titers at day 0, 3, 6, and 9 months.
analysis_trace.indication: COVID-19 seroconversion and immunosenescence in elderly institutionalized population.
analysis_trace.patient_population: Elderly residents (mean age ~86 years) of nursing homes/long-term care units with fragility factors. N=98 actual enrollment.
analysis_trace.target_mechanism: Humoral immune response to SARS-CoV-2 infection; assessment of immunosenescence impact on antibody persistence.
analysis_trace.endpoint_interpretation: Continuous immunogenicity endpoint (neutralizing antibody titers). No binary success threshold defined in protocol. All four timepoints measure same analyte to characterize kinetics.
analysis_trace.safety_analysis: Minimal safety risk from blood sampling. No safety endpoints defined as primary outcomes.
analysis_trace.key_risks: 1) Evidence gap: No direct published results from this trial available by cutoff. 2) Immunosenescence may accelerate antibody decline. 3) Heterogeneous infection timing and severity affects baseline titers.
analysis_trace.evidence_to_prediction: Evidence from Collarino 2022 (PMC9709707) in similar elderly LTCF population (n=91, mean age 86) shows: anti-S titers stable over 12 months; NAb titers significant decrease between month 3 and 6, then plateau; 88% had detectable NAb at M12; 42.6% maintained NAb >50 AU/mL at M12. Evidence role: indirect_direction (similar population, different site). Evidence from nursing home studies shows antibody persistence is variable but generally detectable at 6-9 months in majority.
analysis_trace.coverage_gaps: No direct NCT04563650 results available. No specific quantitative threshold for 'success' defined. Heterogeneity in infection timing, severity, and immunosenescence markers not fully characterized in available evidence.
